subject.title: feat(cli): improve editor handoffs for agents and humans

question: Should `crabbox/editor-handoff/v1` be accepted as a supported automation interface with the fields and omission behavior proposed by this PR?
rationale: A named versioned schema is a durable public CLI contract; tests can verify encoding but cannot decide the long-term compatibility promise maintainers want to make.

options.title: Approve stable v1 after proof
options.body: Accept the proposed contract once live behavior proof and successful checks confirm the implementation matches the documented lifecycle.

options.title: Mark the contract experimental
options.body: Ship structured output under an explicitly unstable schema or compatibility policy until field semantics have real consumer experience.

options.title: Keep human-only output
options.body: Decline the new automation surface and retain the merged prose handoff until a different agent interface is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve stable v1 after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the proposed contract once live behavior proof and successful checks confirm the implementation matches the documented lifecycle.

likelyOwner.reason: The current editor-handoff abstraction and lifecycle entered main through this person's merged feature work, making them the strongest available owner for its public contract extension.
